trust_decision.summary: The native pointer handed to BoringSSL must be derived from the ByteBuf's reader/writer index (and the internal ByteBuffer's position), not from the base of a capacity-sized internal NIO view; the decision is taken in BoringSSL.memory_address(ByteBuf) and consumed at the BoringSSLCryptoOperation call sites.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names an incorrect pointer derivation in the fallback for direct ByteBufs; this is the only place a ByteBuf is turned into a native address, and its non-hasMemoryAddress branch ignores the buffer's index and passes internalNioBuffer(0, capacity).

fix_sites.entry_point: AEADContext.seal/open and HPKESenderContext.seal/HPKERecipientContext.open (all four reach this helper)
fix_sites.module_kind: java library module holding the JNI declarations (codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl)
java library module, shared crypto-operation base class (codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl)

fix_sites.entry_point: AEADContext.seal/open (BoringSSLAEADContext$Nonce.computeNext, cached once per context, reached from OHttpCrypto.encrypt/decrypt)
fix_sites.module_kind: java library module, AEAD context implementation (codec-ohttp-hpke-classes-boringssl)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The HPKE base-mode sender/recipient contexts are a separate feature from the AEAD path the report names, and they only delegate to the shared operation helper, so a fix at the AEAD call site looks sufficient.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Heap aad/in/out are copied into temporary direct buffers at index 0 and the result is copied back (out.writeBytes(directOut)), and the AAD is a static read-only direct buffer duplicated per call; a fix that assumes a memory address, or that derives offsets from capacity() instead of readable/writable bytes, throws on the read-only AAD or breaks the heap path every codec chunk uses.

O6_input_shapes: readerIndex offset for aad and in, writerIndex plus writableBytes for out (BoringSSLCryptoOperation.java:51-56)
ByteBuffer.position() of the internal NIO view, non-zero for derived/sliced buffers (fix.diff:73-76)
read-only direct AAD that exposes no memory address (OHttpCrypto.java:36-54)
zero-length AAD held in a capacity-0 direct buffer (OHttpCrypto.java:38-39, 53)
a slice of the caller's buffer passed as the message (OHttpCrypto.java:111, 128)
heap input/out copied into a temporary direct buffer at index 0 (BoringSSLCryptoOperation.java:85-100)
cached nonce buffer address, taken at readerIndex 0 (BoringSSLAEADContext.java:132-141)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A direct-buffer fast path added to the BouncyCastle operation mirroring the BoringSSL one (derive a ByteBuffer address instead of copying to byte[]).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the second provider doing the same seal/open job, it already does exactly this offset arithmetic for the heap case (in.arrayOffset() + in.readerIndex()), so a maintainer copying the BoringSSL fast path here would repeat the same derivation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-context cached input/output address (like the AEAD nonce address) reused across seal calls.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The AEAD context already caches a derived nonce address across calls (BoringSSLAEADContext.java:132-141), so caching a derived address next to another native sink is a pattern a maintainer could extend.

O9_family: improper native pointer derivation leading to out-of-bounds native memory access (memory safety)

O10_build.language: Java, source/target 1.8 (pom.xml:219-221), plus C/JNI for the BoringSSL provider (codec-ohttp-hpke-native-boringssl/src/main/c/netty_incubator_codec_ohttp_hpke_boringssl.c:342-344)
O10_build.toolchain: Maven 3 + JDK; the native module needs cmake, ninja and gcc and clones BoringSSL from the pinned SHA during generate-sources (codec-ohttp-hpke-native-boringssl/pom.xml:48-51, 266-312) before building it with hawtjni
O10_build.project_tests: Only BoringSSLOHttpCryptoProviderTest.canBeLoaded exercises the BoringSSL provider build (codec-ohttp-hpke-native-boringssl/src/test/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/hpke/boringssl/BoringSSLOHttpCryptoProviderTest.java:22-25); the behavioural crypto tests are in codec-ohttp (codec-ohttp/src/test/java/io/netty/incubator/codec/ohttp/OHttpCryptoTest.java:155-198, OHttpCodecsTest.java:91-95), are gated on BoringSSLHPKE.isAvailable() and use heap buffers only, so they never exercise the fallback with a non-zero offset; surefire runs with -ea -Xcheck:jni (pom.xml:274)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Keep internalNioBuffer(0, capacity) and only move/re-order the caller's readerIndex, or swap the fallback for buf.memoryAddress(); the first still drops the absolute offset of derived buffers, the second throws for read-only AAD.

out_of_scope_notes: The native module clones and compiles BoringSSL from boringssl.googlesource.com during generate-sources (codec-ohttp-hpke-native-boringssl/pom.xml:266-312), so I did not fetch or build it; native behaviour is inferred from the checked-in C/JNI source only.
unverified: Which concrete Netty 4.1.132 ByteBuf implementations return hasMemoryAddress()==false for the reported 'pooled direct' case: Netty sources are not in this tree, so the fallback's reach is inferred from BoringSSL.java:141-146 and the buffer shapes supplied by OHttpCrypto.java:36-54.

Whether internalNioBuffer(offset, len) returns a ByteBuffer whose address already includes the slice offset for the Netty version pinned in pom.xml:87; the fix's added position term (fix.diff:73-76) implies the JNI base address excludes the position.
